It's a figure of speech. As it then says,

As such, we cannot engage them in the same way that we engage the other ‘players’. The war against the Artists is, unfortunately, waged on their home turf. While they throw us the occasional skip, most of what they make is not directed towards us. It is released into the wild, presented as ‘art’, and then summarily forgotten.

If a group like the Chaos Insurgency is directly attacking the Foundation, they can figure out where the attack is coming from and fight back. The problem with the Artists is that they aren't 'attacking', they're just showing stuff to some people and leaving before the Foundation can react.

item.content:encoded: Skips sounds sort of like SCP and the spelling indicates a similar sound. The main difference is that one is an acronym with no vowels, and the other is a slang word with a vowel. Reasons why people might use “skip” instead of “scip”: auto-correct, spell check, and skip might be slightly more intuitive in pronunciation.

item.content:encoded:
Yes.

Number one, this fits my AWCY headcanon. They aren't an organization, a group or even a collective, they're a movement, and this agent has every right to call them a "fad". They condense into cells, they have different concepts of approaching the same idea, they have different goals and methods. What unites them is a catchphrase and what they produce.

Second, I'd just recently been thinking that treating AWCY as a group, with The Critic and all that, actually makes tales less interesting. Granted, I've been enjoying Ruiz's exploits, but that's because he's sticking it to those idiots that I've come to dislike. I don't mind it when that group is used, but people have to not think of them as the center of AWCY, or even a representative majority. They're just one highly visible, highly powerful group among many.

Lastly, this is a great orientation. I like the bits about breaking Foundation code. I especially like the part about the agents having to make their own skips. You're really treating AWCY as the threat they are, both not as bad and worst than how most tend to use them. Well done.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Now, for the tale itself: I generally loathe the idea of destroying skips, but with AWCY…there really isn't a viable alternative, is there? They're producing them at a rate that would bankrupt even the Foundation eventually, because it's not just resources expended to -capture- it. It's also keeping it somewhere. And all the employees, paperwork, construction and such needed for the object. So we'd have to start destroying some of them rather than containing if we want to continue operations for any significant amount of time.
